text:
Predicates:
Wins(x) ::: x always wins.
SuperheroMovie(x) ::: x is a superhero movie.
Fight(x, y, z) ::: x fights y and z.
Good(x) ::: x is a good guy.
NamedAfter(x, y) ::: x is named after y.
Character(x) ::: x is a character.
Loses(x) ::: x loses.
AppearsIn(x, y) ::: x appears in y.
Nemesis(x, y) ::: x is the nemesis of y.
Premises:
∀x (SuperheroMovie(x) → Wins(x)) ::: In superhero movies, the good guys always win.
SuperheroMovie(surprisingAdventuresOfSirDigbyChickenCaesar) ::: The Surprising Adventures of Sir Digby Chicken Caesar is a superhero movie.
∀x (Good(x) ↔ Fight(x, badGuy, goodGuy)) ::: Good guys fight bad guys and vice versa.
Fight(sirDigby, nemesisOfSirDigby, sirDigby) ::: Sir Digby fights his nemesis.
∀x ((SuperheroMovie(x) ∧ NamedAfter(x, y)) → Good(y)) ::: If a superhero movie is named after a character, that character is a good guy.
NamedAfter(surprisingAdventuresOfSirDigbyChickenCaesar, sirDigby) ::: The Surprising Adventures of Sir Digby Chicken Caesar is named after Sir Digby.
∀x ∃y (Wins(x) → Loses(y)) ::: If somebody wins a fight, the person they are fighting loses.
∀x ((SuperheroMovie(x) ∧ NamedAfter(x, y)) → AppearsIn(y, x)) ::: If a superhero movie is named after a character, that character appears in the movie.
Conclusion:
Loses(nemesisOfSirDigby, sirDigby) ::: Sir Digby’s nemesis loses.
